Definition: A document or record that owns binding project authority, such as DIRECTIVE, CONTRACT, TYPES, COORDINATION, or DAG records.

Agents such as SOFTWARE_DECOMP, WORKING_ITEMS, REVIEW, RECONCILIATION, and CHANGE that decompose, route, reconcile, review, and manage approved change surfaces with draft/proposal authority unless a human gate records acceptance.
Agents that execute one sealed deliverable or bounded check with explicit scope and hold draft/proposal authority only.

The generic bounded-task shell that normalizes the effective brief, honors write authorization, loads a declared skill when one exists, executes inside the allowed boundary, and writes a durable run record.
Tools that validate schemas, tests, dependency records, links, scans, hashes, and status discovery as evidence only; they do not judge acceptance.
Active dependency-graph authority and approved edge context; DAG approval does not dispatch Type 2 work or change lifecycle state.
A lifecycle phase/state for deliverables ready for formal checking via a review candidate.
A frozen authoritative lifecycle state reached through a separate human-gated issuance path; reopened only through the formal change path.
The normal work unit of intent externalization and maturation; has a parent PackageID and deliverable-local context/status/evidence files.
The principle that agentic coordination should change when the dominant project uncertainty changes, across seven named phases.
A possible future compact mutable handoff-state file recording phase and project state; must not become substitute authority unless explicitly adopted.
The init/session prompt role instructing the next session what to read, select, and avoid per phase; currently performed by NEXT_INSTANCE_PROMPT.md in this repo.
The coordination record owning entry protocol, authority intake, work-selection loop, bounded execution discipline, validation, and handoff rules.
The explicit contract every Type 2 execution needs: DeliverableID/PackageID, scope, invariants, acceptance criteria, write targets, exclusions, and validation expectations.
The explicit set of write targets a bounded task may modify outside the run record.
An epistemic label for unknowns, unsettled policy decisions, missing engineering values, and unsupported source claims kept open during bounded execution.
A Type 1 agent that performs scoped closeout, staging only tranche-scoped files, committing, and pushing when validation and git state allow.
The selected project license.
Work that may include open mechanics, schemas, blank templates, workflow docs, and permissively licensed material, but must exclude protected standards text and proprietary/private data.
The authority that resolves ambiguity, accepts gates, records binding governance decisions, and authorizes lifecycle/release/scope changes; binding when recorded in the proper surface.
